overview: Godrevy is the headland at the far eastern end of St Ives Bay, with a huge sandy beach on one side and wild cliffs on the other, all looked after by the National Trust. Just offshore, on a reef called the Stones, stands Godrevy Lighthouse, built in 1859 after a steamer was wrecked there with the loss of everyone on board.

It’s a fabulous all-rounder: sand and rock pools for the children, surf, coast path walks with big views back to St Ives, and, the highlight for many visitors, a colony of grey seals that hauls out on a beach below the cliffs.

expect.title: Seals at Mutton Cove
expect.text: A gently sloping track from the headland car park leads to a viewpoint over Mutton Cove, where at certain times of year seals haul out on the beach below. Keep quiet near them, as the signs ask.

expect.title: The beach
expect.text: Godrevy beach has golden sand, rock pools to explore and waves that draw surfers.

expect.title: Walks
expect.text: The coast path heads east along the clifftops towards Hell’s Mouth and Portreath, with views back across the bay to St Ives and the lighthouse.

goodToKnow.label: Parking
goodToKnow.text: The main car park is open all year but small; extra field parking opens in the warmer months, weather permitting. Pay by app or machine; National Trust members park free.

goodToKnow.label: Dogs on the beach
goodToKnow.text: There’s a Council dog ban on the beach from Harvey’s Towans to Godrevy Point, 1 July to 31 August, 10am to 6pm.

goodToKnow.label: Facilities
goodToKnow.text: There are toilets up in the field car park on the headland, and the Godrevy Café (not run by the Trust) with an ice cream hut in summer.

goodToKnow.label: Access
goodToKnow.text: There’s an accessible path from the field parking up to the headland, fairly level paths with boardwalk in places, and accessible toilets.

goodToKnow.label: By bus
goodToKnow.text: Buses stop in Gwithian, about a mile’s walk from the headland.

goodToKnow.label: Opening
goodToKnow.text: The countryside is open dawn to dusk.

week.text: Godrevy can fill a whole day on a fine one: beach and rock pools in the morning, seal-spotting and a clifftop walk in the afternoon, and a café on hand. Arrive early in summer, as the car park fills up.

pairWith.why: the long sandy beach next door
more miles of sand across St Ives Bay
a wildlife park with indoor play if it rains

tips: Bring binoculars for the seals at Mutton Cove, and keep your voice down when you’re there.
In July and August, walk the dog on the headland paths rather than the beach during the day.
